rubriker.title: US Championships: Shankland and Woodward score
rubriker._rss_content: Wesley So and Awonder Liang drew their direct encounter in round three of the US Championship, remaining tied for first place on 2½/3. Andy Woodward and Sam Shankland (pictured) scored victories, with Woodward joining Fabiano Caruana half a point behind the leaders. In the women's tournament, Alice Lee defeated Nazi Paikidze to join Thalia Cervantes and Megan Paragua in first place. Defending champion Carissa Yip suffered her second consecutive defeat. | Photo: Lennart Ootes / Saint Louis Chess Club

rubriker.title: Yu Yangyi beats Ding Liren in final match, wins Shenzhen Masters
rubriker._rss_content: At the Shenzhen Masters, China's leading players faced young talents. The matches were contested in a knockout format, with four rapid games per encounter. In the event of a draw, blitz tiebreaks decided the matches. Defending champion Ding Liren faced Yu Yangyi in the final match. After a lengthy battle, Yu Yangyi came out on top. | Photos: Chinese Chess Association

rubriker.title: Yu Yangyi gana el Shenzhen Masters tras vencer a Ding Liren en la final
rubriker._rss_content: En el Shenzhen Masters, algunos de los ajedrecistas más fuertes de China se enfrentaron a jóvenes talentos. Los encuentros se disputaron mediante un sistema de eliminatorias, con cuatro partidas rápidas por enfrentamiento. En caso de empate, se recurrió a desempates a ritmo blitz. El defensor del título, Ding Liren, se enfrentó a Yu Yangyi en la final. Tras una prolongada lucha, Yu Yangyi se impuso para quedarse con el título. | Fotos: Asociación China de Ajedrez

rubriker.title: A dispute in the Bundesliga
rubriker._rss_content: The German Chess Bundesliga is known for its continuity. For decades, it has operated under well-established rules, although players, spectators and arbiters have not always agreed on how to apply them. A particularly curious case arose in the 1986/87 season: A match started late, raising the question of whether a grandmaster had arrived on time. What followed was a furious battle over the rules, a series of appeals, a replayed match, a relegation play-off and repeated changes to which team would be relegated. | Photo: Dr Robert Hübner playing in the Bundesliga in the 1980s (All photos courtesy of Eising and Treppner, Schachbundesliga)

Fagernes: Jumabayev takes title, Gloeckler secures second GM norm
rubriker._rss_content: Fourteen-year-old Christian Gloeckler secured his second grandmaster norm at the International Autumn Tournament in Fagernes, Norway. Although the German youngster lost his final two games, this did not affect the norm he had already secured. Rinat Jumabayev, Tiger Hillarp Persson and G. B. Harshavardhan (pictured, left) shared first place with 7½/10 points each. | Photo: Anniken Vestby

rubriker.title: Supratit Banerjee, 12, Becomes Youngest International Master in British Chess History
rubriker._rss_content: Twelve-year-old Supratit Banerjee has made history by becoming Britain's youngest-ever International Master (IM), breaking a record previously shared by grandmasters Luke McShane and David Howell.

rubriker.title: German Blitz Chess Championships to Be Broadcast Live on ARD and ZDF in 2027
rubriker._rss_content: Chess will make its debut at Germany's prestigious multi-sport event, The Finals, with the national blitz championships set to receive live coverage on the country's two major public television broadcasters, ARD and ZDF

rubriker.title: FIDE's General Assembly Backs Shorter Classical Time Controls
rubriker._rss_content: FIDE's General Assembly has formally supported a resolution on shorter classical time controls.

rubriker.title: La Olimpiada que no fue reconocida por la FIDE: Múnich 1936
rubriker._rss_content: Entre todas las Olimpiadas de Ajedrez celebradas a lo largo de la historia, el torneo de 1936 en Múnich ocupa un lugar especial. La FIDE no reconoció oficialmente el evento como una Olimpiada de Ajedrez. Sin embargo, la competición entre selecciones nacionales cumplía todos los requisitos. Al igual que en 2026, el equipo alemán también consiguió la medalla de bronce en aquella ocasión. | Fotos: Ferenc Chalupetzky / Libro del torneo
